title: connection-linger-heap-leak-and-intermittent-partial-output-reconciliation
creator: Asha Patel
description: High-severity customer reports: several Hosted API streaming sessions (SSE) are returning truncated/partial outputs or duplicate tail tokens after a short TCP/TLS pause. Postmortem investigations show increased process memory over time on a subset of fronting proxies causing delayed session close and stale fragment re-emission; this manifests differently across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private configurations. This ticket coordinates an engineering fix + rollout + customer communications.
background: Multiple enterprise customers (support tickets #CS-12844, #CS-12902, #CS-12911) reported: (1) generated responses missing the final sentence or final token, (2) clients reconnect and see a duplicate suffix or repeated tokens, and (3) occasional 502s during bursts followed by stale partials. These started rising two weeks ago after a traffic pattern change introduced by a partner integration. Observable in prod: fronting-gateway processes with long-lived connections show heap growth and deferred sentinel emission. Existing stream resume heuristics attempt to stitch fragments but assume the server-side final token marker was always emitted.
observed_behavior: 1) Idle network glows (~2s TCP stall) -> fronting proxy delays connection close -> backend continues to produce tokens (KV cache growth) but final-token sentinel not committed to client. 2) Client reconnects and resumes; Stitcher sees overlapping fragments and either drops a suffix (partial output) or replays trailing tokens when the delayed emit finally arrives. 3) Memory on gateway climbs ~20-30% on the affected pool over 6-12 hours leading to evictions and recoveries that correlate with customer complaints.
root_cause: A combination: (A) a latent heap retention bug in fronting-gateway's SSE buffer handling that retains per-session fragment buffers until GC; (B) stream commit semantics assumed eventual synchronous final-token marker emission; (C) resume logic lacks a stable, monotonic final-sentinel confirmation and therefore misattributes late-emitted fragments as duplicates rather than missing suffixes.
proposed_fix: 1) Fix buffer lifecycle: immediately free per-session buffers on connection termination events (edge-case path where proxy kept socket state after TLS rekey). 2) Strengthen commit protocol: introduce an opaque final-sentinel nonce that servers include in the final chunk and persist in the session index; resume RPC must validate nonce monotonicity before stitching. 3) Add an ack/confirm handshake for critical terminal chunks when client supports it; fall back to legacy behavior for older SDKs. 4) Backfill tooling: implement a safe reassembly utility that can be run for affected customer sessions to replay missing suffixes where we still have fragments in storage.
rollout_plan: - Week 1 (canary): Deploy buffer-lifecycle fix to a 5% fronting-gateway pool in us-west-2; enable increased mem/alloc metrics and a custom debug flag to surface orphaned fragments. - Week 1 (canary): Deploy final-sentinel nonce change behind a feature flag for hosted runtime; no default consumption unless client flags present. - Week 2: Monitor for 72 hours; if no regression, promote to 25% then 100% over 48 hours. - Week 2 (compat): Release SDK patch (node/python) to interpret final-sentinel and perform commit-ack. - Week 3: Run reassembly backfill for impacted customer windows; provide opt-in resume restore for enterprise customers. - Communications: notify active escalations at start of canary, mid-canary, and full rollout completion.
testing_plan: Unit tests for buffer free paths covering connection-termination + TLS rekey scenarios
Integration test: simulated 2s TCP stall -> final-token emission late; ensure resume logic yields deterministic output after nonce validation
Chaos test: kill fronting-gateway worker mid-stream and verify no orphan memory retained and session index consistency
Load test: 10k concurrent streams with synthetic stalls to validate memory behavior and latency SLOs
SDK compatibility tests across Node/Python/Go: ensure fallback path for older clients remains unchanged
telemetry_and_alerts: Query: count(streams where final_sentinel_received=false and connection_close_time - final_emit_time > 5000) by gateway_pool
Alert: frontend_heap_growth_rate > 10% over 1h for more than 3 hosts in a pool -> P0 pager
Dashboard panels: per-tenant partial-output-rate, duplicate-suffix-rate, avg-time-between-final-and-close
SLO health: streaming_success_rate 99.9% (daily window) - create ephemeral alert if < 99.5%
mitigations: Customer-side temporary workaround: set client-side resume window to 1s (less aggressive) to avoid mis-stitching late fragments
Ops mitigation: recycle fronting-gateway pool nightly in affected regions until fix is deployed
API toggle: server-side feature flag to force immediate buffer free on close (non-default) to reduce leak impact for escalated tenants

decision_log: 2026-03-14: Decided to fix buffer lifecycle in the gateway first to stop memory growth before protocol changes (Asha, Miguel, Priya)
2026-03-15: Agreed to add final-sentinel nonce (opt-in feature flag) to avoid breaking older SDKs (Miguel, Ryan)
2026-03-15: Backfill tooling scoped as opt-in for enterprise customers only due to storage/consistency trade-offs (SRE/Product)
Trade-offs: introducing nonce plus ack increases network traffic slightly and adds complexity to the resume flow but makes outputs deterministic and auditable
